title: The Weak child in the bed
subtitle: 身体健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）
meta: 主题语境：身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）　|　核心词汇：weak　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 weak 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1982 the director wrote of ① a weak child in the bed in the poster, and everybody in the theatre said at once that it was ② weaker than the one named there the year before. Three nights on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the director, who never explained anything, had done it with great care and gone home; it was the weak ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the weakest child in the bed anybody in the theatre had ever seen, or so the poster for August 1976 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too weak to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the actor who had come to help; the weak ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the script at the far stage, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a weak point of the plan, and said that no actor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as weak as the point of the plan they had once had in the old theatre. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was weak or not, and he said so.

By 1989 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the poster. What the line asked for was ⑦ something weak, and nothing besides. The actor from the next theatre called the whole plan ⑧ quite weak; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the poster kept the names of the weak ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1992, on the same day, she wrote of another weak child in the bed in the same poster, and the work, which took two nights, seemed ⑨ weaker than anybody had expected. ⑩ The weakest point of the plan in the whole theatre, she said in 1994, was the one she could never quite name; the weak ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 虚弱（前置定语 a weak child in the bed：1982 年导演在戏报里记下的那件虚弱的孩子）
B. adj. 虚弱／薄弱（比较级 weaker than：文中两处，一处比床上虚弱的孩子，一处比预想）
C. adj. 虚弱／薄弱（最高级 the weakest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 虚弱（表语 too weak to do：母亲觉得它太虚弱，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 薄弱（前置定语 a weak point of the plan：叔叔把整件事称作一桩薄弱的环节）
F. adj. 薄弱（同级比较 as weak as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩方案中的薄弱环节相比）
G. adj. 薄弱（后置定语 something weak：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 薄弱（受程度副词修饰 quite weak：那位演员的评价）

items.q: a weak child in the bed
the weakest child in the bed anybody
a weak point of the plan
The weakest point of the plan in

answers.why: weak 意为“虚弱”，1982 年导演在戏报里记下的是“一件虚弱的孩子”，此处作前置定语 a weak child in the bed。
weak 意为“虚弱”，此处用比较级 weaker than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
weak 意为“虚弱”，戏报上 八月 那行字说它是戏院里最虚弱的一件，故用最高级 the weakest child in the bed。
weak 意为“虚弱”，母亲认为这件东西“太虚弱了，谁也用不上”，too weak to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
weak 意为“薄弱”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩薄弱的环节”，此处作前置定语 a weak point of the plan。
weak 意为“薄弱”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩方案中的薄弱环节一样薄弱”，同级比较用 as weak as。
weak 意为“薄弱”，戏报上那半行字要的是“薄弱的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something weak。
weak 意为“薄弱”，邻戏院来的那位演员认为这套计划“相当薄弱”，quite 修饰原级 weak。
weak 意为“薄弱”，1992 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要薄弱”，故用比较级 weaker than。
weak 意为“薄弱”，母亲 1994 年说的是“整个戏院里最薄弱的那一桩”，故用最高级 the weakest point of the plan。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1982 年，导演在戏报里记下了一件虚弱的孩子。（a weak child in the bed）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更虚弱。（weaker than …）
母亲觉得它太虚弱，谁也用不上。（too weak to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩薄弱的环节。（a weak point of the plan）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩方案中的薄弱环节一样薄弱。（as weak as …）
到了 1989 年，戏报上只剩半行字：要的是一件薄弱的东西。（something weak）
answers: In 1982 the director wrote of a weak child in the bed in the poster.
Everybody said it was weaker than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too weak to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a weak point of the plan.
He said nobody would call it as weak as the point of the plan they had once had.
By 1989 the poster asked for nothing but something weak.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 weak 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1982 the director wrote of a weak child in the bed in the poster, and nobody forgot it.
It was the weakest child in the bed in the theatre, or so the poster says.
My mother thought it too weak to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a weak point of the plan, and nobody argued with him.
The actor from the next theatre called the plan quite weak, and everybody laughed.
The weak ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
